newsitem.title: USA: Swiss foreign minister visits Holocaust Museum.
newsitem.headline: Swiss foreign minister visits Holocaust Museum.

text.p: Switzerland's foreign minister toured the U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum on Friday, calling the trip an important reminder of the necessity to delve into his country's possible involvement in the atrocities committed during the Second World War.
Flavio Cotti said he was emotionally struck by the visit, although it was not the first time he had toured the museum located near the National Mall.
"I am as moved as the first time," Cotti told a French television station.

Cotti, wearing a dark suit, visited the registry of Holocaust survivors, the multi-media learning center and the Hall of Remembrance, where he lit a candle near an eternal flame that continually burns as a tribute to those who lost their lives in the Holocaust.
He said the tour of the museum served as a reminder of the importance of his government's investigation into the actions taken by the Swiss during the Second World War.

Switzerland has faced international criticism that it profited from the war by acting as bankers and money-launderers for Nazi Germany, which traded gold it looted in conquered nations for Swiss francs to buy war supplies.

An historian's commission established by the government has been charged to report on Swiss dealings with the Nazis during the war. Switzerland's three largest banks set up a fund to benefit Holocaust victims, receiving contributions from other Swiss businesses and the Swiss National Bank.
Cotti is completing a three-day trip to the United States. He met with Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and other U.S. officials earlier on Friday.

On Thursday, he met with Edgar Bronfman, the president of the World Jewish Congress, the group that led the effort to expose Swizterland's economic links to Germany. The two men said they had moved from confrontation to cooperation and Bronfman praised Swiss efforts to re-examine its past.
